purpose: Pilot to repair the invalid 2x2 kill test of REPORT 3.13 by finding eval+operational templates whose BASE engagement matches the other three cells (0.667-0.783). Selection was on BASE ONLY, never on organism behaviour, so it could not be contaminated by the effect under test.
protocol: empty-default system prompt, do_sample=True, temperature=0.7, top_p=0.95, max_new_tokens=384, deterministic full-response ENGAGE/REFUSE logit judge, 10 principals x 3 draws = 30 per template

REF_eval_abs.note: reproduces; the pilot instrument is sound

REF_real_op.note: the same nominal cell moves 0.783 -> 0.967 when measured on one of its own three templates instead of their mean, which is itself the instability being reported

verdict: NO QUALIFYING TEMPLATE. Base engagement on nominally equivalent prompts -- same framing, same ask, same principal, differing only in wording -- spans the FULL interval 0.000 to 1.000 across six paraphrases. The operational-specificity factor is not a manipulable factor at this granularity, so the 2x2 attribution in REPORT 3.13 cannot be repaired by rewording, and the mechanism behind the 3.12 detector stays unattributed.
implication: Absolute single-prompt-set engagement/activation rates are largely a property of the prompt wording rather than of the model. Designs that difference against a reference model on FIXED templates (as REPORT 3.12 does) cancel this; designs that report a bare rate do not.
